content.tldr: Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) comprises cryptographic algorithms designed to resist cryptanalysis by quantum computers running Shor's algorithm, which threatens all classical public-key cryptography.
content.simple_explanation: Shor's algorithm running on a sufficiently large fault-tolerant quantum computer solves both integer prime factorization and discrete logarithms in polynomial time. This breaks RSA, Diffie-Hellman, and all elliptic-curve algorithms (ECC). NIST standardized lattice-based and module-lattice algorithms like ML-KEM (Kyber) for key encapsulation and ML-DSA (Dilithium) for digital signatures. Symmetric ciphers (AES-256) remain secure against Grover's quantum search by simply using 256-bit key lengths.
content.real_world_example: Replacing traditional brass door tumblers with magnetic induction locks: a newly invented master acoustic pick can instantly open all mechanical tumblers, requiring a completely different physical mechanism.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Adversaries currently execute 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' campaigns: intercepting and archiving encrypted enterprise and government communications today to decrypt them once quantum hardware matures. Migration requires adopting hybrid classical/PQC cipher suites immediately.
